searchText: Just peered with a node reporting these protos: `"eth/62", "eth/63", "eth/64", "eth/65", "wit/0"` -- what's the `wit/0`? It's a `Nethermind/v1.10.12-0-c6362932e-20210205/X64-Linux/5.0.2` cc <@!489256758989029405> witness sync protocol for stateless beam naive witness -> list of hashes of trie nodes that were read in the current block execution we serve up to 256 recent witnesses which allows beam sync to process blocks in miliseconds hmmm just realized that mainnet has now around 90 nodes supporting wit/0 😮 should try to use https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/328fe83deee15b35b14ab4b005575370eff578f3/caps/wit.md if you could build servers for wit/0 <- this would help it took my one day of coding for the server side, depending on some client specific things it could take a bit more - maybe up to a week depending on the architecture specific challenges I do not think that it much overhead 256 * maybe 0.5mb 120mb of witnesses then we could add them to block headers to avoid false witnessing (not a huge problem now anyway) (block header with a hash of concatenated witness hashes) it is so super simple that it is easier than to have a single discussion on the 'advanced witness' ideas and can be easily upgraded later when improvements come very compatible with many things that we talk about and very lightweight we can present the beam sync internals on one of the calls
